locator: I q.105 a.5 co.: the second always acts in virtue of the first
interpretation: Second of the three ways God works in every agent: 'where there are several agents in order, the second always acts in virtue of the first; for the first agent moves the second to act.' Read as a general principle about ordered agents: a second agent's acting is from its being moved to act by the first, with no restriction to a respect of its being moved. It is about agents generally, not only about the movers of ST I q.2 a.3, and it is stated for an order of agents, so it is positive evidence for, not a restatement of, the strong per se premise STMT-SECOND-MOVERS-MOVE-ONLY-AS-MOVED. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
